source.title: AdamL: A fast adaptive gradient method incorporating loss function

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: It compares optimizer variants on held-out metrics for image classification and language modeling, using a different optimizer and experimental setup from the claim's cited studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy and test perplexity for optimizer comparisons. Its CNN accuracy results are described in text but shown as figures without extractable values. Benchmark-function convergence results do not measure generalization. No natural-label versus random-label comparison, interpolation-width sweep, batch-size comparison, dropout or weight-decay ablation, sharpness measure, or memorized-example removal test is reported.
record.test_reason: No claim version is tested. The neural-network experiments compare Adam-family optimizers without an SGD or momentum-SGD held-out comparator, so they cannot establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD difference or its recovery. The momentum-GD comparison concerns Rosenbrock optimization, not generalization. No experiments address V1–V3 or V5–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase captures the authors' overall conclusion but needs qualification: AdamL improves convergence and performance in several tasks and achieves the lowest listed LSTM perplexities; peak CNN accuracies are similar among AdamL, EAdam, and AdaBelief for ResNet18 and DenseNet121, and AdamL does not clearly outperform competitors on WGAN-GP. Its CNN procedure avoids late manual learning-rate reductions, but LSTM experiments still require them.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes AdamL and compares it with Adam, EAdam, and AdaBelief; its natural-task tests do not include SGD as a held-out-performance comparator.
record.method_sensitivity: For CNNs, increasing AdamL's γ improved test accuracy but slowed convergence; results also varied by architecture and dataset. LSTM results varied with learning-rate decay schedule and model depth.

fits_no_version.finding: AdamL has the lowest test perplexity in every Table 4 depth and decay-schedule condition. These comparisons include only Adam, EAdam, AdaBelief, and AdamL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AdamL can improve Penn Treebank LSTM test perplexity relative to the compared Adam-family methods under the reported settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.3 reports higher AdamL test accuracy for VGG11, similar peak accuracy among AdamL, EAdam, and AdaBelief for ResNet18 and DenseNet121, and the lowest accuracy for Adam. Increasing AdamL's gamma improves accuracy while slowing convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out image accuracy and convergence depend on the Adam-family variant, architecture, and optimizer settings.

record.problems: Natural-task optimizer comparisons omit SGD or momentum SGD as a held-out-performance comparator. CNN test-accuracy values are presented in figures without exact values in the text. LSTM Table 4 gives mean perplexities but no displayed per-cell maximum deviations, despite the caption mentioning them.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the numeric Table 4 test-perplexity results. CNN test-accuracy findings are described but exact values are figure-only; they are not included as rows because the text does not state the values and the figures do not provide extractable values here.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning; recovery through switching or decoupled weight decay; Adam versus SGD on word-level language models.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that remove them.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: All 24 numerical values and listed depth/schedule conditions match Table 4. Its caption mentions maximum deviations, but no per-cell deviations appear in the supplied table. References to SGD-like update modes do not supply an SGD generalization comparison. Figure-only CNN findings were already declared in rows_left_out and do not warrant missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.
The reported held-out comparisons are among Adam-family variants; the paper does not compare their held-out performance with SGD or momentum SGD on these tasks.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch test.
No sharpness or other generalization-gap measure.
No removal of memorized training examples.
